Where it began

Angus Alexander Patrick Atkinson, known as Gus, was born in Chelsea on 19 January 1998. He went to Northcote Lodge, a prep school in Wandsworth, and then to Bradfield College in Berkshire.

He made his first-class debut for Surrey on 8 August 2020, in the Bob Willis Trophy, and played T20 for them later that month. He was part of the Surrey side that won the County Championship in 2022, and in The Hundred he bowled for the Oval Invincibles.

The player

A right-arm fast bowler, he made his T20 international debut against New Zealand on 1 September 2023 and took 4 for 20, the best by an England man on his T20 international debut. He was picked for the World Cup in India that autumn.

His Test debut, against the West Indies at Lord's on 10 July 2024, was something else. He took seven in the first innings and five more in the second. No England bowler had done better on debut for 134 years than his 12 for 106. By November 2026 he had played 21 Tests, taking 83 wickets at 25.35 with a best of 7 for 45, five five-wicket hauls and one ten-wicket match. With the bat he had 587 runs at 19.57, and 9 catches.

What made him special

Lord's seemed to suit him. Against Sri Lanka there in August 2024 he reached his first first-class hundred in 103 balls, then took five wickets in the second innings. That made him only the third England player to score a hundred and take five in an innings in the same Test, and the first since Ian Botham in 1984. It also made him one of only six players with a hundred, a five-wicket innings and a ten-wicket match at the ground.

That December he took a hat-trick against New Zealand, the first by an Englishman in any Test since 2017. His batting came and went, as a fast bowler's is allowed to, and he averaged 19.57 with it. That innings against Sri Lanka showed what he could do once he got in.

Away from the middle

The awards followed quickly. The Cricket Writers' Club named him England's player of the year for 2024, and he was one of Wisden's Cricketers of the Year in 2025.

And finally

His Test batting record has a lovely shape to it: one hundred and not a single fifty. Once he gets past the awkward middle bit, he clearly sees no point in stopping halfway.
